cases.sentence: Ветерок, который был на езде, затих, когда остановились; слепни облепили сердито отбивавшихся от них ___.
cases.explain: «потных лошадей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The coachman pulled up his four horses and looked round to the right, to a field of rye, where some peasants were sitting on a cart. The countinghouse clerk was just going to jump down, but on second thoughts he shouted peremptorily to the peasants instead, and beckoned to them to come up. The wind, that seemed to blow as they drove, dropped when the carriage stood still; gadflies settled on the steaming horses that angrily shook them off. The metallic clank of a whetstone against a scythe, that came to them from the cart, ceased. One of the peasants got up and came towards the carriage.

cases.sentence: – Ишь рассохся! – сердито крикнул конторщик на медленно ступавшего по колчам ненаезженной ___ босыми ногами мужика. – Иди, что ль!
cases.explain: «сухой дороги» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Well, you are slow!” the countinghouse clerk shouted angrily to the peasant who was stepping slowly with his bare feet over the ruts of the rough dry road. “Come along, do!”

cases.sentence: – Воздвиженское, на ___? к графу? – повторил он. – Вот только изволок выедешь.
cases.explain: «барский двор» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Vozdvizhenskoe, the manor house? the count’s?” he repeated; “go on to the end of this track. Then turn to the left. Straight along the avenue and you’ll come right upon it. But whom do you want? The count himself?”

cases.sentence: – Должно, дома, – сказал мужик, переступая ___ и оставляя по пыли ясный след ступни с пятью пальцами. – Должно, дома, – повторил он, видимо желая разговориться. – Вчера гости еще приехали.
cases.explain: «босыми ногами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “At home for sure,” said the peasant, shifting from one bare foot to the other, and leaving a distinct print of five toes and a heel in the dust. “Sure to be at home,” he repeated, evidently eager to talk. “Only yesterday visitors arrived. There’s a sight of visitors come. What do you want?” He turned round and called to a lad, who was shouting something to him from the cart. “Oh! They all rode by here not long since, to look at a reaping machine. They’ll be home by now. And who will you be belonging to? …”

cases.sentence: Они ездили кататься и смотреть действие вновь привезенных ___.
cases.explain: «жатвенных машин» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: They were Vronsky with a jockey, Veslovsky and Anna on horseback, and Princess Varvara and Sviazhsky in the charabanc. They had gone out to look at the working of a new reaping machine.

cases.sentence: Анна ехала ___ на невысоком плотном английском кобе со стриженою гривой и коротким хвостом.
cases.explain: «спокойным шагом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: When the carriage stopped, the party on horseback were coming at a walking pace. Anna was in front beside Veslovsky. Anna, quietly walking her horse, a sturdy English cob with cropped mane and short tail, her beautiful head with her black hair straying loose under her high hat, her full shoulders, her slender waist in her black riding habit, and all the ease and grace of her deportment, impressed Dolly.

cases.sentence: ___ ее с выбившимися черными волосами из-под высокой шляпы, ее полные плечи, тонкая талия в черной амазонке и вся спокойная грациозная посадка поразили Долли.
cases.explain: «Красивая голова» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When the carriage stopped, the party on horseback were coming at a walking pace. Anna was in front beside Veslovsky. Anna, quietly walking her horse, a sturdy English cob with cropped mane and short tail, her beautiful head with her black hair straying loose under her high hat, her full shoulders, her slender waist in her black riding habit, and all the ease and grace of her deportment, impressed Dolly.

cases.sentence: За ним ехал ___ в жокейском костюме.
cases.explain: «маленький человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: After him rode a little man in the dress of a jockey. Sviazhsky and Princess Varvara in a new charabanc with a big, raven-black trotting horse, overtook the party on horseback.

cases.sentence: Свияжский с княжной в ___ на крупном вороном рысаке догоняли верховых.
cases.explain: «новеньком шарабане» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: After him rode a little man in the dress of a jockey. Sviazhsky and Princess Varvara in a new charabanc with a big, raven-black trotting horse, overtook the party on horseback.

cases.sentence: – Вы не поверите, как мы рады вашему приезду, – сказал он, придавая особенное значение произносимым словам и улыбкой открывая свои крепкие ___.
cases.explain: «белые зубы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “You wouldn’t believe how glad we are to see you,” he said, giving peculiar significance to the words, and showing his strong white teeth in a smile.
